lore.common: Remains on last month until you have missed three appointments. Then looks disappointed.
lore.uncommon: Remembers everyone's birthday except the person holding it. This is always deliberate.
lore.rare: Moves the dentist appointment onto every holiday. The dentist has started booking holidays too.
lore.epic: Ate Monday from the royal calendar and caused a nationwide four-day weekend. The economy survived; the alarm clocks did not.
lore.legendary: Chronomara keeps a hidden month between December and January, where time goes to sleep. Only the children know it exists, and they never tell the teachers.

names.legendary: Fridalia, the Page That Stole Spring

lore.common: Curls up in the corner so you can never tell whether today is Wednesday or Thursday.
lore.uncommon: Gets torn off early by someone desperate for Saturday. It remembers and holds a grudge.
lore.rare: Swaps the picture of June with a blizzard. The office has begun wearing scarves in summer.
lore.epic: Tore seven days off itself in one furious flutter. By breakfast the entire school believed Christmas was tomorrow.
lore.legendary: Fridalia tore a single Friday from the calendar of the gods and folded it into eternity. Somewhere, an office has been enjoying the same long weekend for a thousand years.

names.legendary: Sir Formsworth, Supreme Inspector of All

lore.common: Snaps its metal clip on a finger and immediately records the incident as operator error.
lore.uncommon: Gives anyone holding it the confidence of a health inspector. Even the mayor starts tidying.
lore.rare: Produces new checkboxes whenever someone finishes the old ones. The list is gaining power.
lore.epic: Stormed the town hall with an army of paperwork and declared every citizen overdue for an inspection. The pigeons failed on hygiene.
lore.legendary: Sir Formsworth's clipboard contains the master checklist of the universe. The last unticked box reads COMPLETED EXISTENCE, and he keeps asking for a signature in triplicate.

names.legendary: Memorix, Keeper of the Unwritten Truth

lore.common: Opens itself to the page with the most embarrassing doodle.
lore.uncommon: Loses its tiny key just before somebody has a very important secret.
lore.rare: Writes back in the margins with observations nobody remembers telling it.
lore.epic: Leaked the royal court's private gossip into every town noticeboard. The gossip was so accurate the king appointed it historian.
lore.legendary: Contains every confession never spoken aloud. Once each century Memorix grants one person the courage to read their own story, even the chapter they tried to erase.

lore.common: Drops an important page every time somebody carries it upstairs.
lore.uncommon: Changes its label whenever a colleague claims to have organised the office.
lore.rare: Sorts documents by emotional importance. Bills go under Terrifying, birthday cards under Urgent.
lore.epic: Led every file folder in the building out of its cabinet and into the boardroom. The directors were formally buried in their own paperwork.
lore.legendary: Archivella filed the first royal secret under M for Mysterious. Centuries later nobody remembers the secret, but every librarian still fears opening that drawer.

lore.common: Snaps its elastic strap at anyone who tries to close it neatly.
lore.uncommon: Bulges with worksheets no student has willingly read.
lore.rare: Swallows tonight's homework and spits out last year's timetable instead.
lore.epic: Exploded on the school bus and sent a year's worth of worksheets spiralling into the sky. The pupils claimed it was an educational meteor shower.
lore.legendary: Folderoth grew so full of forgotten assignments that it developed its own memory, a timetable and a strong opinion about exams. The headteacher made it an honorary pupil.

lore.common: Fills its first page with elaborate doodles because writing the date feels like too much effort.
lore.uncommon: Closes itself whenever someone tries to read the owner's secrets over their shoulder.
lore.rare: Writes down brilliant ideas in the night that its owner hasn't thought of yet. By breakfast they seem obvious.
lore.epic: Opened during a thunderstorm and released a hundred paper doors, each leading into a different adventure its owner had forgotten.
lore.legendary: Wanderquill records the memories of travellers who never returned. When its pages turn in the wind, their loved ones hear the sound of footsteps coming home.

names.legendary: Professor Pagewell, Keeper of Every Idea

lore.common: Catches its wire binding in a jumper sleeve just as the teacher looks over.
lore.uncommon: Runs out of paper in the middle of the most important sentence. The pen feels betrayed.
lore.rare: Copies all the doodles from neighbouring desks and hides them between the algebra notes.
lore.epic: Opened itself the night before the final exam and sent every student's forgotten revision notes fluttering back to their desks. Nobody understood how the stapler got involved.
lore.legendary: Pagewell kept the unfinished ideas of a hundred inventors between its pages. Each time someone opens it to a blank sheet, one lost idea finds a new mind.

lore.common: Makes little spirals and angry faces during every telephone call. Claims it's taking minutes.
lore.uncommon: Writes the shopping list beautifully, then leaves itself on the kitchen worktop when everyone goes to the supermarket.
lore.rare: Turns CALL GRAN into COOL GORILLA. The family has stopped asking it to take messages.
lore.epic: Rearranged every note in the office so the accountant attended the plumber's birthday and the plumber chaired the annual budget review. Both did surprisingly well.
lore.legendary: Scribbleton once wrote a message so illegible that the words escaped into the world to find their own meaning. They returned as a story no pen could have invented.

lore.common: Organises the week's chores with twelve pens, then forgets to do the washing up.
lore.uncommon: Schedules tea, snacks and rest breaks so tightly that there is no time to enjoy them.
lore.rare: Squeezes an extra hour into every Saturday. Nobody can explain why the clock looks so nervous.
lore.epic: Booked the mayor for seventeen meetings at once and somehow made him attend every one. The city declared Monday a public holiday.
lore.legendary: Schedulora once fitted an entire year's worth of celebrations into a single perfect day for a village facing its final winter. No one missed a birthday, not even the oldest clockmaker.

lore.common: Snaps its rings shut just as a finger reaches between them.
lore.uncommon: Eats every punched hole from its pages, leaving a small snowdrift of paper circles.
lore.rare: Grows new dividers that lead the reader into subjects never taught at school.
lore.epic: Unleashed a thousand sheets of paperwork into the town hall, each one demanding a signature from the mayor.
lore.legendary: Bindoria bound every broken promise of the royal court into one immense ring binder. When the rings sprang open, the paperwork buried the throne.

lore.common: Falls off the monitor every time someone finishes writing an important reminder.
lore.uncommon: Sticks to the cat instead of the fridge, and the cat now has a shopping list.
lore.rare: Duplicates urgent notes whenever a deadline approaches, until the entire office whispers 'Buy milk'.
lore.epic: Covered every window of the city hall in yellow reminders so thickly that the council accidentally voted to buy six thousand bananas.
lore.legendary: Memorina keeps one last message from a civilisation that vanished before paper existed. Whenever someone forgets a kindness, the note appears on their door.

lore.common: Wobbles whenever someone takes a book from the bottom. It considers physics optional.
lore.uncommon: Sags under encyclopaedias and blames modern literature for the weight.
lore.rare: Opens into a secret passage when the correct book is tilted. Its favourite book is never the one you think.
lore.epic: Knocked over one volume and started a domino cascade through twelve libraries. The librarians are still shushing the rubble.
lore.legendary: Behind its oldest books are doors into forgotten stories. Bibliomaw lets brave readers enter, but insists they return books on time.

lore.common: Turns to mush after meeting a single raindrop. Calls it structural flexibility.
lore.uncommon: Becomes a castle, spaceship or dinosaur with one enthusiastic child and a roll of tape.
lore.rare: Transforms into a sled the moment it sees a snowy hill. The landing is always optional.
lore.epic: Built an entire cardboard metropolis overnight. The cats took control of the government before breakfast.
lore.legendary: Corrugon built a palace from the discarded boxes of kings. It survived three wars, one flood and a thousand moving days, then surrendered to a glass of orange juice.

names.legendary: Orizuru, Herald of the Folded Sky

lore.common: Has one wing higher than the other and flies in extremely sincere circles.
lore.uncommon: Flaps its folded wings whenever someone pulls its tail, then acts offended at the string.
lore.rare: Carries a tiny wish beneath its paper beak and releases it only when the fold is perfect.
lore.epic: Led a squadron of paper cranes out of the classroom and across the city, delivering forgotten invitations to a wedding nobody could find.
lore.legendary: Orizuru was folded from a letter written by two enemies who wished for peace. It crossed the storm between their cities and returned with a second letter tucked beneath its wing.

lore.common: Hides the important letter beneath three takeaway menus.
lore.uncommon: Seals its flap before the letter is inside. Calls it a security feature.
lore.rare: Returns to sender whenever anyone lies about having posted a birthday card.
lore.epic: Convinced every envelope in the post office to deliver itself. By lunchtime the streets were full of paper pigeons and very frightened stamps.
lore.legendary: Crossed oceans, wars and four generations to deliver an apology nobody remembered writing. The old house opened its own letterbox and cried a single drop of ink.

names.legendary: Signoria, Who Named the Nameless Road

lore.common: Points left on Mondays and right on Tuesdays, confusing the poor delivery driver.
lore.uncommon: Collects stickers from tourists and wears them like medals from foreign countries.
lore.rare: Reveals the true name of any road it stands beside, including paths forgotten by every map.
lore.epic: Switched every street name in the capital for one night. By dawn the mayor lived on Pickle Parade and the palace was on Duck Lane.
lore.legendary: Signoria named a path through a forest no traveller had crossed. Every lost soul who reads her letters sees the road that leads them home.

lore.common: Hides the country you need between two pages. It opens to Greenland whenever anyone asks about the weather.
lore.uncommon: Folds maps into impossible shapes and insists the tiny paper boats are sovereign nations.
lore.rare: Its maps change while nobody is looking. One cartographer woke to find his bedroom had been reassigned to Iceland.
lore.epic: Spilled coffee across its pages and accidentally created a new continent. Three empires immediately argued over the stain.
lore.legendary: Atlastrix carries maps of places that have not yet been discovered. Every time it turns a page, an island is born, a lost road returns or a daring explorer realises they're standing upside down.

lore.common: Unfolds to the size of a blanket and refuses to return to pocket size.
lore.uncommon: Insists that north is wherever its owner happens to be facing.
lore.rare: Reveals a tiny path nobody has ever noticed before, leading straight to a very good tea shop.
lore.epic: Redrew all the streets during the mayor's grand tour. The marching band visited every garden in town before reaching the square.
lore.legendary: Cartographus charts the routes of places that disappear at dawn. Once each century, the map opens a road to a kingdom that exists only in memory.

lore.common: Leaves grey thumbprints on every white sofa in town. Calls this journalism.
lore.uncommon: Lets grandad finish the crossword in pen before anyone else gets a chance.
lore.rare: Prints tomorrow's gossip in tiny headlines beneath today's weather. The mayor has started reading it under a blanket.
lore.epic: Whirled every Sunday edition into the air and covered the town in flying front pages. People caught headlines about themselves that had not happened yet.
lore.legendary: Tomorrow's Herald carried news of a flood a full day before the river rose. Ever since, its blank final page has waited for the story that no one can yet bear to read.

lore.common: Spits a bird's nest of thread under the fabric, then looks innocent while the needle snaps.
lore.uncommon: Sewed the family tablecloth to someone's sleeve and insists it is the newest fashion.
lore.rare: Stitches fabric so quickly that a torn dress repairs itself before it reaches the floor.
lore.epic: Sewed a thousand costumes for a royal masquerade in a single night. At dawn, every guest had been dressed as the king, including the king.
lore.legendary: Singerella stitches the futures of unborn fashions into one endless ribbon. When she sewed a missing moonbeam back into the night, the stars demanded matching hems.

names.legendary: Punchella, the Hole in the Heavens

lore.common: Spills a hundred tiny paper circles onto the floor, then watches its owner try to collect them.
lore.uncommon: Takes three sheets at once and acts as though it has just conquered a mountain.
lore.rare: Punches holes in perfect geometric patterns across homework. The teacher suspects secret messages.
lore.epic: Perforated an entire library of books during one very enthusiastic office party. Readers now use the holes as miniature windows.
lore.legendary: Punchella punched a single round window through the thickest storm cloud in history. Sunlight shone through onto a lost village, and the villagers named the opening after her.

lore.common: Prints a label reading LABEL and sticks it on itself for reassurance.
lore.uncommon: Calls the sugar SUGRA and the flour FLOWER. It is proud of its spelling.
lore.rare: Labels a cupboard EMPTY and, to everyone's horror, the biscuits disappear.
lore.epic: Labelled every object at a village fair, including the mayor, the fountain and a passing cloud. The mayor has been known as LUNCH ever since.
lore.legendary: Nomenclara prints a name for anything that has never had one. When it labelled the silence after a snowstorm, the whole valley whispered the word in unison.

lore.common: Snaps at paper corners and pretends it is a tiny crocodile.
lore.uncommon: Removes a staple but eats the top left corner of the page as a tip.
lore.rare: Pulls the staples from every noticeboard at once, releasing an avalanche of important announcements.
lore.epic: Unfastened every page in the royal records overnight. The kingdom woke up with its laws rearranged in alphabetical order.
lore.legendary: Unstaphel removed the final clasp from an ancient spellbook, freeing every unfinished story trapped between its pages. The librarians have barricaded the doors.

names.legendary: Adhesar, Binder of the Broken Road

lore.common: Shouts SKREEEE every time someone packs a birthday present quietly.
lore.uncommon: Tapes the box closed before the gift has been put inside.
lore.rare: Shoots adhesive strips around runaway furniture and reels it back toward the moving van.
lore.epic: Sealed every door in the warehouse in one magnificent sweep, forcing the delivery drivers to leave by the loading ramp.
lore.legendary: Adhesar stitched a shattered mountain bridge with a single ribbon of silver tape, allowing the last caravan to cross before the dawn. The tape still holds the morning mist in place.

names.legendary: The Last Tender, Sovereign of Change

lore.common: Refuses to unfold properly at the till. The queue is beginning to take sides.
lore.uncommon: Gets folded into an origami swan and then demands interest on the art supplies.
lore.rare: Can escape any wallet and reappear in the pocket of whoever genuinely needs a sandwich.
lore.epic: Printed itself one extra zero and purchased the town hall. The mayor must now pay rent in loose change.
lore.legendary: Has passed through the hands of kings, thieves and generous strangers. It always returns to its first owner on the day they need it most.

lore.common: Flutters just enough to turn WELCOME into WELC OME. The guests take the hint.
lore.uncommon: Catches the wind so hard it drags two chairs and a very surprised uncle down the street.
lore.rare: Changes its message whenever nobody looks. The last village festival was mysteriously sponsored by ducks.
lore.epic: Unfurled across the valley and summoned every forgotten parade in history. The traffic police requested immediate retirement.
lore.legendary: Carried a lost kingdom's colours for a thousand years. When Vexilla rises, even ruined castles remember how to stand tall.

names.legendary: The First Testament, Guardian of Ages

lore.common: Turns its wafer-thin pages with a dramatic little sigh whenever someone rushes the reading.
lore.uncommon: Holds pressed flowers between its verses. Each one remembers who placed it there.
lore.rare: Opens itself at an old family inscription whenever a forgotten name is spoken aloud.
lore.epic: A single line glowed from its ancient pages and lit the church through a week-long blackout. The candles asked for a holiday.
lore.legendary: Across generations, its margins hold births, farewells and prayers. When the last family name is read aloud, every faded hand appears in gold upon the page.

lore.common: Bites the nearest thumb whenever anyone squeezes its little metal ears.
lore.uncommon: Folds its silver wings like a tiny insect about to launch a very small rebellion.
lore.rare: Can clamp a thousand sheets into one indestructible brick. Paperwork has officially become masonry.
lore.epic: Bound all the reports in the office into a single towering manuscript. The boss needed a crane to sign it.
lore.legendary: Held an entire collapsing skyscraper together with one black jaw. The building was saved, though every document inside was filed alphabetically.

lore.common: Rattles with the unmistakable sound of money. Opens to reveal a drawing of money.
lore.uncommon: Sings Happy Birthday when opened. Its battery has outlived three house moves and a divorce.
lore.rare: Releases glitter that cannot be cleaned. Archaeologists will one day date the house from it.
lore.epic: Started singing inside a postbox and infected every card in the district. The sorting office became the world's least organised musical.
lore.legendary: Writes congratulations for birthdays that haven't happened yet. Its latest card reads HAPPY 300TH, and the recipient is only six.

names.legendary: The Lectern That Held a Sleeping God

lore.common: Lets the cookbook fall closed at the exact moment the cook covers both hands in flour.
lore.uncommon: Grips pages so aggressively the recipe now includes a thumbprint garnish.
lore.rare: Refuses to release any book before its last sentence is read. Students have started smuggling shorter novels.
lore.epic: Held every recipe in the kingdom open at once. The kitchens cooked themselves into a glorious twelve-course disaster.
lore.legendary: For a thousand years it held the same book open while its reader slept. When the god finally woke, the stand gently asked for a bookmark.

names.legendary: Atlashelf, the Unfallen Pillar of Words

lore.common: Slides along the shelf every time another book is added. Insists it is a strategic retreat.
lore.uncommon: Looks like a small elephant and lands on feet with the confidence of an actual elephant.
lore.rare: Squeezes books so tightly that their fictional characters end up in one another's chapters.
lore.epic: Held up the entire library after the shelves vanished during renovation. The librarian called it efficient space planning.
lore.legendary: When libraries burn or kingdoms crumble, Atlashelf keeps their last book standing. It remembers every story, including the ones their authors never finished.

names.legendary: Manualoth, Prophet of the Missing Step

lore.common: Stabs the person reading it with its staple. This is described in the safety section.
lore.uncommon: Curls up at the corners whenever somebody tries to photograph the instructions.
lore.rare: Hides the one useful instruction until after the furniture has been assembled incorrectly.
lore.epic: Made a wardrobe-building guide so confusing that the family accidentally constructed a second bathroom. The plumber gave it five stars.
lore.legendary: Manualoth knows how every machine works but deliberately omits step seven. Entire civilisations have fallen over the phrase SOME ASSEMBLY REQUIRED.

names.legendary: Marginalia, Guardian of the Final Page

lore.common: Falls out of the book the moment its owner falls asleep. It calls this an escape.
lore.uncommon: Saves your place in an entirely different novel. The plot now includes three detectives and a dragon.
lore.rare: Moves ten pages backward every night. The reader has learned the first chapter by heart.
lore.epic: Rearranged every bookmark in the library at once. Three hundred readers woke convinced they had dreamed the same ending.
lore.legendary: Marginalia guards the last page of every unfinished story. Those who find her may read the ending, but must promise never to spoil it.

names.legendary: Brochurella, Siren of the Unbooked Isles

lore.common: Lands on your doormat promising sunshine. The forecast outside is rain.
lore.uncommon: Has pages so glossy that every holiday picture also includes your worried reflection.
lore.rare: Makes the beach on its cover look so inviting that the reader starts packing before checking the price.
lore.epic: Projected a tropical sunset from a bus shelter so bright the entire town got a tan. The council is suing for sunscreen.
lore.legendary: Brochurella tempts travellers with places that exist only between her folded pages. Those who find them send postcards home, always with the same mysterious stamp.

lore.common: Stares back at the artist until they panic and paint a bowl of fruit.
lore.uncommon: Drinks every colour it is offered and burps out a muddy brown. Art critics call it daring.
lore.rare: Turns accidental splashes into portraits of people you have not met yet.
lore.epic: Escaped the art studio and painted the entire town in the style of a furious toddler. Property prices unexpectedly doubled.
lore.legendary: Artifex paints creatures that climb out of their frames and demand names. Its masterpiece is a blank canvas that knows exactly what will happen tomorrow.

lore.common: Hangs at a slight angle no matter how many times the nail is straightened.
lore.uncommon: Insists it is an original masterpiece despite being printed at a discount shop.
lore.rare: Copies anyone who stops to admire it into the background. Dad is now immortalised behind the Mona Lisa.
lore.epic: Replaced every painting in the gallery with pictures of its own face. The critics called it an important commentary on identity.
lore.legendary: Fauxelle has impersonated the greatest paintings for centuries. When the original artists came to complain, she printed them as limited editions.

lore.common: Makes a sound like a thousand tiny screams whenever somebody writes the number eight.
lore.uncommon: Leaves white fingerprints on everything except the blackboard where they belong.
lore.rare: Draws doors on walls and sometimes remembers to make them real. The caretaker is furious.
lore.epic: Sketched a maze of hopscotch squares across the entire city. Traffic stopped while the children conquered every intersection.
lore.legendary: Chalkazar drew the first city on a cave wall and the walls became streets. Every rainstorm tries to erase his work, so he keeps an umbrella made of dust.

lore.common: Screeches when a fingernail touches it. The entire class suddenly remembers an appointment elsewhere.
lore.uncommon: Coughs white dust onto the teacher's black jumper whenever somebody says clean.
lore.rare: Keeps yesterday's answers faintly visible. Students call it their wisest classmate.
lore.epic: Shook off a century of chalk dust in one great sneeze. The classroom vanished into a white cloud and emerged with tomorrow's exam completed.
lore.legendary: Professor Obsidian remembers every lesson ever erased from its surface. It can teach forgotten languages, extinct mathematics and the true identity of whoever stole the class hamster.

names.legendary: Lord Tarwick, Duke of Borrowed Breaths

lore.common: Clings to clothes for days after leaving the room. Nobody invited it to stay.
lore.uncommon: Promises a moment of peace and delivers an ashtray smell to the entire house.
lore.rare: Whispers just one more from the bottom of a packet. Its negotiating skills are unfortunately excellent.
lore.epic: Blanketed the royal masquerade in stale smoke until every guest fled into the rain. The baron's disguise was still obvious from the smell.
lore.legendary: Lord Tarwick once convinced a kingdom it needed his smoke to feel free. When the last citizen put him out, he shrank to a dusty speck and nobody missed the crown.

names.legendary: King Stubulus, Emperor of the Last Drain

lore.common: Hides between paving stones where every broom misses it. Smug little nuisance.
lore.uncommon: Clogs gutters with its cousins and acts surprised when the street floods.
lore.rare: Multiplies along the beach whenever nobody is looking. The tide refuses to take it, and the crabs have formed a cleaning brigade.
lore.epic: Built an entire fortress of discarded filters beneath the promenade. A beach-cleaning robot laid siege and won in seven minutes.
lore.legendary: Stubulus claimed the world's drains as his rightful empire. His glorious reign ended when one very determined street sweeper arrived with a dustpan and absolutely no respect.

lore.common: Turns every serious speech bubble into a squeak. The superhero is losing credibility.
lore.uncommon: Hides the final page whenever its reader reaches a cliffhanger. Charges extra for closure.
lore.rare: Makes sound effects leap off the page. The library now has a permanent THWACK problem.
lore.epic: Released its illustrated villains into the city during a convention. Everyone thought they were cosplayers until the speech bubbles blocked traffic.
lore.legendary: Inkarion draws doorways through the walls of reality. It can give any hero a happy ending, but always insists on a dramatic cliffhanger before the credits.

lore.common: Opens itself at the one recipe missing an ingredient.
lore.uncommon: Has three pages stuck together with chocolate. They are the only good recipes.
lore.rare: Quietly substitutes salt for sugar in the royal chef's notes, then asks to judge dessert.
lore.epic: Its recipes came alive and staged a coup in the kitchen. The souffles demanded voting rights; the soup declared martial law.
lore.legendary: Contains the last recipe of a vanished civilization. Nobody knows the final ingredient, but every cook who reads it suddenly craves a second helping.

lore.common: Gets declined whenever the checkout queue is long enough to require snacks.
lore.uncommon: Whispers, It's basically free, beside anything wildly overpriced.
lore.rare: Makes purchases invisible until the statement arrives, escorted by tiny thunderclouds.
lore.epic: Bought the mayor's statue, the town hall and its own debt collection agency in a single contactless tap.
lore.legendary: Wields the ancient power of Buy Now, Regret Forever. Even dragons, famous for hoarding gold, hide their wallets when Creditorax visits.

lore.common: Steals one loop from every project and hides it in the sofa.
lore.uncommon: Hooks strangers' scarves together as they pass. Public transport becomes very intimate.
lore.rare: Can unravel a jumper with one gesture, then crochet it into a suspiciously accurate cat.
lore.epic: Worked through one sleepless night and crocheted a sweater for the entire village. It has only one armhole.
lore.legendary: Crocheted a net large enough to hold a falling star, then patiently stitched its light into the night sky. The star has never thanked her.

names.legendary: Lexicor, Author of the Last Word

lore.common: Opens at precisely the wrong word and insists the reader learn it anyway.
lore.uncommon: Corrects people's pronunciation from inside a closed schoolbag.
lore.rare: Invents a new insult so elegant that even the person being insulted applauds.
lore.epic: Added one outrageous word to every official speech in the kingdom. Parliament spent a month debating what flibberconstitutional meant.
lore.legendary: Wrote the first name ever spoken and remembers the last word yet to be said. Its pages grow whenever anyone discovers a feeling language cannot describe.

names.legendary: Easelion, Witness of the First Dawn

lore.common: Loses its footing whenever the painter declares the picture finished.
lore.uncommon: Grips the canvas too tightly and leaves two dents shaped like angry eyebrows.
lore.rare: Can keep a painting upright through an earthquake, but falls over when a cat sneezes.
lore.epic: Held a canvas steady while a storm painted the entire town onto it. The mayor tried to hang the picture in city hall; the clouds objected.
lore.legendary: Easelion stood beneath the first sunrise while the world was painted into color. Every painting it supports contains one tiny glimmer from that impossible morning.

lore.common: Occupies a whole shelf just to explain the word shelf.
lore.uncommon: Sneezes whenever someone opens Volume Q. Nobody has identified the allergy.
lore.rare: Answers every question correctly, then whispers an embarrassing fact about the person who asked.
lore.epic: The volumes marched into the council chamber and corrected every politician simultaneously. The meeting ended after three hours of people asking what a fact was.
lore.legendary: Knows the answer to a question nobody has thought to ask. Once every century it opens to that page and waits for humanity to catch up; meanwhile it moonlights as a doorstop.

names.legendary: Vexilla, the Banner of Lost Kingdoms

lore.common: Wraps around its own pole whenever anyone tries to take a photograph.
lore.uncommon: Snaps in the wind like it is applauding a joke nobody else heard.
lore.rare: Can signal a message across the sea with one flap. Unfortunately, it usually says LUNCH.
lore.epic: Tore free during the village parade and flew ahead of the marching band, leading them into the rival town's wedding. Both celebrations merged by accident.
lore.legendary: Vexilla carried the colours of a kingdom long erased from maps. When the forgotten people gathered beneath it again, their homeland appeared in the morning mist.

names.legendary: Flyerion, Herald of the Lost Cat

lore.common: Tucks itself beneath a windscreen wiper and flaps for the entire commute.
lore.uncommon: Arrives through the letterbox before breakfast, even when nobody has delivered it.
lore.rare: Can spread news across the whole town by riding every gust of wind. The news is usually about a missing umbrella.
lore.epic: Plastered a LOST CAT notice on every lamp post overnight. By morning the whole town was searching, including the cat, who wanted to know what the fuss was about.
lore.legendary: Flyerion carried a faded notice across generations until someone finally recognised the face on it. The lost cat had become the mayor and was refusing to answer questions.

names.legendary: Prittoria, Keeper of the Last Page

lore.common: Leaves its cap behind after every art lesson. The cap has begun writing farewell letters.
lore.uncommon: Dries out the moment someone leaves the cap off. Has been rehearsing its farewell speech for years.
lore.rare: Glued every worksheet in the class into a single paper dragon. It now flies round the ceiling, correcting spelling mistakes.
lore.epic: Joined every worksheet in a classroom into one magnificent paper dragon. The pupils demanded a school mascot.
lore.legendary: Prittoria glued the final page of a lost story back into its book. The characters stepped out to thank her and refused to return until she promised a sequel.

names.legendary: Postoria, the Card That Arrived Before

lore.common: Arrives two days after your birthday and has the nerve to say many happy returns.
lore.uncommon: Collects so many signatures that nobody remembers whose birthday it is.
lore.rare: Rewrites the message inside whenever someone opens it. The boss's retirement card now says congratulations on your new puppy.
lore.epic: Unfolded into a birthday message the size of the town square. The mayor had to read it from a hot-air balloon.
lore.legendary: Postoria delivered a farewell note to a traveller before he had decided to leave. He stayed home instead, and the card still sends him postcards.

names.legendary: Clawdia, Keeper of the Royal Curls

lore.common: Snaps onto hair with a noise loud enough to wake the bathroom mirror.
lore.uncommon: Clings to one stubborn strand and drags an entire hairstyle sideways.
lore.rare: Can seize a runaway ponytail from three feet away like a tiny silver crab.
lore.epic: Snatched up every wig at the royal costume ball and stacked them into a tower. The queen attended dinner with a peacock on her head.
lore.legendary: Clawdia held the princess's impossible curls through a hundred-year storm. When the wind stopped, every cloud overhead had acquired a perfect fringe.

lore.common: Lives on a wrist for months and insists it has never been used to tie hair.
lore.uncommon: Springs off a ponytail during the school race and launches itself into the crowd.
lore.rare: Vanishes from every drawer but appears whenever someone's hair has finally been cut short.
lore.epic: Stretched across the ballroom and tied every dancer into one giant ponytail. Nobody wanted to be first to leave.
lore.legendary: Loopella is the only hair tie the Lost Things Kingdom cannot steal. She returns every missing partner to its wearer, though sometimes it comes back attached to a dragon.

lore.common: Disappears from the dressing table and turns up between the sofa cushions. Again.
lore.uncommon: Keeps a delicate bun in place until exactly the moment a photograph is taken.
lore.rare: Can hold a hairstyle together through a whole thunderstorm. Afterwards the wearer looks like a very angry umbrella.
lore.epic: Secured an entire theatre curtain with one tiny pin. The standing ovation pulled the wall down instead.
lore.legendary: Pinella once plucked a thorn from a lion's paw with its slender tip. The lion crowned it guardian of his mane and has never tolerated a bad haircut since.

lore.common: Falls around your ankles after exactly two heroic spins.
lore.uncommon: Rolls away across the playground and returns wearing someone else's skipping rope.
lore.rare: Spins fast enough to lift its wearer off the ground, turning every dance lesson into flight school.
lore.epic: Escaped sports day and rolled through the whole town, collecting runners, cyclists and one police officer inside its spinning circle.
lore.legendary: Hoopla once encircled the great festival grounds and kept a thousand dancers moving until sunrise. The ring still hums with their footsteps whenever the wind blows.

lore.common: Chooses the least flattering photo from a thousand attempts and wears it proudly.
lore.uncommon: Twists around on its lanyard just when a security guard asks to see it.
lore.rare: Opens a door that has never recognised anyone else. Refuses to explain its clearance level.
lore.epic: Locked every executive out of their own office and let the cleaner run the company for a day. Productivity immediately improved.
lore.legendary: Credentia once opened a door that had not moved in a hundred years. Behind it waited the founder's forgotten lunch, still warm and remarkably smug.

lore.common: Drops a perfect little tower of ash and acts surprised when someone sneezes it over.
lore.uncommon: Bends its smoke into question marks whenever someone says the room smells strange.
lore.rare: Guides lost visitors through a winding house by leaving a scented trail in the air.
lore.epic: Burned at the entrance to the village market and scented every street at once. The baker staged a protest because nobody could smell his bread.
lore.legendary: The Last Ember burned through an entire winter without shortening an inch. Its smoke led travellers through the blizzard to the doors of a mountain shrine.

lore.common: Clicks out a secret rhythm during television programmes, and the remote has started keeping time.
lore.uncommon: Drops one stitch in every jumper to give it a little window for the wind.
lore.rare: Knits a scarf that slithers behind its owner and coils around anyone who mentions the cold.
lore.epic: Knitted blankets for the entire village overnight. By dawn every rooftop wore a woollen hat, and the chimney sweeps were furious.
lore.legendary: Grandmother Knitrix spins frost into wool at the first snowfall. Legends say she once knitted an entire winter short so a lost child could get home before dark.

names.legendary: Sir Laminalot, Sealer of the Ages

lore.common: Traps one enormous air bubble in every document and calls it its signature.
lore.uncommon: Takes longer to warm up than the kettle takes to make three cups of tea.
lore.rare: Wraps a flimsy paper map in an armour of plastic so rain cannot rewrite the route.
lore.epic: Laminated every certificate in the school, then the desks, then a very surprised principal. The whole building is now wipe-clean.
lore.legendary: Sir Laminalot sealed the last map of a lost kingdom beneath a crystal-clear coat. Storms and centuries passed, but the paths still shine, waiting for someone brave enough to follow them.

lore.common: Draws a red dot across the carpet and pretends it does not see the cat charging after it.
lore.uncommon: Holds still on the wall until the cat pounces, then moves one millimetre to the left.
lore.rare: Can convince a room full of cats that the same dot belongs to each of them.
lore.epic: Led a hundred cats across the grand ballroom with one bouncing red speck. The dancers applauded from atop the chandeliers.
lore.legendary: The Uncatchable Speck travels across walls, moons and mountains, pursued by the first cat that ever saw it. The chase has lasted a thousand nights, and neither would dream of stopping.

lore.common: Crawls beneath the doormat where nobody will read it until next spring.
lore.uncommon: Escapes from the magazine and flutters dramatically into the cereal bowl.
lore.rare: Folds itself into a paper hat on the head of anyone who considers throwing it away.
lore.epic: Promised free pizza on every doorstep in town. By sunset the pizzeria had hired the fire brigade to knead dough.
lore.legendary: One forgotten leaflet invited the citizens of a sleepy kingdom to a meeting nobody expected to attend. Every citizen arrived, and they quietly elected the village cat king.

names.legendary: Quillora, the Letter That Found Home

lore.common: Makes straight handwriting drift slowly downhill until the last line falls off the page.
lore.uncommon: Drinks too much fountain-pen ink and turns every full stop into a little moon.
lore.rare: Rewrites the greeting in every official letter to My Dearest, causing considerable confusion at the bank.
lore.epic: Sent a letter from every schoolchild to their pen pal on the same afternoon. The post office needed a second building just to sort the envelopes.
lore.legendary: Quillora carried a message between two lost friends for so many years that kingdoms changed and roads vanished. When the letter finally arrived, the ink was still wet and the reply was already waiting.

names.legendary: Libellon, Keeper of the True Horizon

lore.common: Its bubble refuses to sit exactly in the middle, even on the flattest table in the house.
lore.uncommon: Announces that a shelf is crooked only after the final screw has been tightened.
lore.rare: Can detect the lean of a house from a single breath, though it still gets confused by the cat.
lore.epic: Ordered every crooked shelf, chimney and chair in town to straighten itself. By morning the leaning tower was a straight tower and the tourists were furious.
lore.legendary: Libellon carries the first perfectly level line ever drawn. When the sea grew wild around a lost fleet, it laid that line upon the waves and gave the sailors one calm road home.

lore.common: Falls over whenever someone gently removes a magazine from the middle.
lore.uncommon: Keeps a celebrity interview from fifteen years ago on top and insists it is breaking news.
lore.rare: Buries the one issue you're looking for at the bottom, then quietly moves it back after you've given up.
lore.epic: Grew through the ceiling of the dentist's waiting room and published its own headline: LOCAL PAPERWORK REACHES THE CLOUDS.
lore.legendary: Stackminster has printed every forgotten tomorrow and preserved every outdated prediction. On its thousandth page, the future is still described as 'coming soon'.

names.legendary: Kurokami, the Hero Beyond the Final Page

lore.common: Opens from the other end and lets first-time readers think they have already spoiled the ending.
lore.uncommon: Stops at the worst cliffhanger, then hides the next volume behind the sofa.
lore.rare: Leaps between ink panels when nobody is looking, leaving sound effects on the furniture.
lore.epic: Escaped its own page borders during a school reading club and turned the entire classroom into a black-and-white chase scene.
lore.legendary: Kurokami defeated the final villain and stepped beyond the last page, carrying every unfinished story in a folded paper sword. Nobody knows which chapter contains the way home.

lore.common: Has a mysterious stain beside the starters that nobody wants to identify.
lore.uncommon: Changes the daily special precisely after everyone has finally decided what to order.
lore.rare: Adds new choices whenever a customer looks uncertain, until the kitchen needs a second building.
lore.epic: Convinced every wedding guest to order the same pudding, then revealed the kitchen had only one spoon.
lore.legendary: Chef Menufesto once wrote the name of a meal so beautiful that an empty table filled itself with its scent. The diners dined on the story and demanded seconds.

names.legendary: Archivor, the Mountain of Forgotten Days

lore.common: Sits beside the recycling bin, confidently predicting that tomorrow will be the day it finally leaves.
lore.uncommon: Wraps itself in string so tightly that nobody can retrieve the sports page.
lore.rare: Grows taller every time someone says they will sort it out on the weekend. The car has moved out of the garage.
lore.epic: Collapsed during spring cleaning and buried the neighbourhood under twenty years of old headlines. The village rediscovered three missing bicycles.
lore.legendary: Archivor stacked every newspaper ever forgotten into a tower touching the clouds. At its summit lies the one edition that printed a story nobody has lived yet.

lore.common: Starts as a paper crane and somehow ends up looking like a disappointed cabbage.
lore.uncommon: Hops across the desk as a tiny frog whenever homework is mentioned.
lore.rare: Changes into whichever animal the room most needs. It was a very unhelpful rhino during the fire drill.
lore.epic: Folded itself into a thousand paper beasts overnight. They marched through the school hall and demanded a wildlife sanctuary.
lore.legendary: Senfold knew the forbidden crease that could give paper a heartbeat. He used it to make a crane that carried a lonely child's letter across the sea without once getting wet.

lore.common: Spits out twice as much paint as anyone requested and calls that artistic enthusiasm.
lore.uncommon: Glues its cap tight when the painter needs one last dot of blue.
lore.rare: Squirts across the canvas in perfect lines to spell an embarrassing secret.
lore.epic: Exploded beneath an artist's boot and covered the gallery floor in a masterpiece no critic dared to step on. The mop received a lifetime ban.
lore.legendary: Tubella held a colour no one had ever seen. When an old painter finally squeezed out one drop, the grey statues of the city turned to watch the sunset.

lore.common: Stares at visitors from its frame as if judging their choice of shoes.
lore.uncommon: Tilts sideways when nobody looks, then denies moving a single millimetre.
lore.rare: Changes the face in its portrait each midnight to resemble whoever last praised it.
lore.epic: Stepped out of its frame and took a guided tour of the museum. The other paintings complained that their tickets had been forgotten.
lore.legendary: The Unfinished Monarch was painted without a crown and spent three centuries searching for one. When a child drew a paper crown on the frame, the kingdom in the painting finally awoke.

lore.common: Drops its middle page the instant the reader gets interested.
lore.uncommon: Appears in every letterbox the morning after someone says they hate junk mail.
lore.rare: Makes a perfect stranger enthusiastically volunteer for a very complicated committee.
lore.epic: Inspired such a heated debate about the village fountain that even the pigeons demanded speaking time. The meeting lasted until the water ran out.
lore.legendary: Pamphletius carried a message across a silent kingdom where speech was forbidden. By sunrise, its tiny printed words had become a thousand people asking to be heard.

lore.common: Gets bent into a tiny heart during meetings and immediately loses its spring.
lore.uncommon: Links arms with every paper clip in the drawer until the chain reaches the door.
lore.rare: Slips into the smallest diary lock and opens it, but only to read the embarrassing doodles.
lore.epic: Summoned a thousand metal clips into a glittering serpent that wound through the office, tying every overdue report neatly together. The manager fainted with relief.
lore.legendary: Clipver held together the last pages of a peace treaty through a hurricane. The ink washed away, but the two rulers remembered the clasp and shook hands anyway.

names.legendary: Captain Crease, Voyager of the Open Sky

lore.common: Dives directly into the floor after its owner promises it will soar.
lore.uncommon: Performs a dramatic loop and lands squarely in the teacher's tea.
lore.rare: Finds the one current of air that reaches the far end of the school corridor.
lore.epic: Flew out of a classroom window and led a whole flock of birds in formation. The head teacher received a postcard from the clouds.
lore.legendary: Captain Crease flew across an ocean with a handwritten message folded into his wings. Years later he returned, salt-stained but still carrying the answer.

lore.common: Slices a finger with one corner, then pretends it was only trying to shake hands.
lore.uncommon: Stares back at a writer until every brilliant idea leaves the room.
lore.rare: Absorbs spilled ink and rearranges it into a completely different message.
lore.epic: Escaped the printer as a blizzard of white sheets, blanketing the office and burying the annual budget. Everyone called it a productivity improvement.
lore.legendary: Vellura kept the stories that no one had dared write. Each night a sentence appeared across her surface, and by morning forgotten people had names again.

names.legendary: Lord Reamarch, Keeper of Endless Pages

lore.common: Feeds five sheets into the printer when the sign clearly asks for one.
lore.uncommon: Leans dangerously beside the desk until someone reaches for the bottom page.
lore.rare: Produces exactly one extra sheet whenever a deadline is announced. Nobody can find a stapler.
lore.epic: Fell across the town council meeting in a monumental wave of paperwork. The councillors were rescued by a clerk with a hole punch.
lore.legendary: Lord Reamarch recorded every promise made in a forgotten kingdom, filling a tower from cellar to roof. When its rulers denied their words, the tower opened like a book and read aloud.

lore.common: Makes a loud crackling noise just as someone tries to turn the page secretly.
lore.uncommon: Fades every photograph except the truly dreadful family haircuts. Those become sharper each year.
lore.rare: Restores a lost memory whenever someone slips an old photo between its pages. The whole family ends up telling stories.
lore.epic: Opened at the annual reunion and projected every embarrassing childhood photograph onto the town hall walls. Nobody escaped the slideshow.
lore.legendary: Memoria holds photographs of families before they were even born. For a century every nervous bride has checked its pages and found a happy wedding portrait waiting.

names.legendary: Framewyn, Guardian of the Last Portrait

lore.common: Falls face down every time someone closes a door. The family thinks it is shy.
lore.uncommon: Gathers a thick layer of dust on the one day visitors are coming.
lore.rare: Changes its photograph's expression to match the room. The wedding portrait currently looks deeply unimpressed.
lore.epic: Replaced every family photograph in the mansion with pictures of the cat wearing different hats. Nobody has managed to reverse the spell.
lore.legendary: Framewyn hung empty for a hundred years. One evening every ancestor appeared inside it at once to complain that the living family had moved the piano.

names.legendary: Foliofox, Guardian of the First Tale

lore.common: Turns its own pages whenever a toddler tries to show someone the pictures.
lore.uncommon: Asks for just one more reading and keeps the entire household awake past midnight.
lore.rare: Lets the painted animals step into the nursery after lights-out. They always put their toys away before morning.
lore.epic: Opened its pages at story time and released a dragon, a prince and forty-seven argumentative frogs. The school library required a second door.
lore.legendary: Foliofox guards the first bedtime story ever told. When a child is afraid of the dark, its pictures glow and the hero of that tale quietly takes watch beside the bed.

names.legendary: Aureframe, Portal of the Painted Age

lore.common: Leans a little to the left no matter how often its owner straightens it.
lore.uncommon: Reflects the window instead of the portrait, which it considers modern art.
lore.rare: Makes a child's messy drawing look like a priceless masterpiece. The museum curator is taking notes.
lore.epic: Swallowed an entire gallery's paintings and replaced them with portraits of itself. Visitors applauded the bold new exhibition.
lore.legendary: Aureframe held a portrait painted before the kingdom existed. Anyone who looks into its glass sees the same street a thousand years earlier, bustling with people who can see them back.

names.legendary: Lady Pinprick of the Silver Needles

lore.common: Looks like a miniature hedgehog that has made several questionable life decisions.
lore.uncommon: Wears a tomato disguise so convincing that the kitchen guests keep reaching for it.
lore.rare: Reclaims every lost sewing pin from the carpet, then lines them up in military formation.
lore.epic: Raised an army of sewing needles to defend the tailor's shop. The invading moths surrendered without touching a single coat.
lore.legendary: Lady Pinprick held together the wedding gown of a princess whose kingdom had no thread. Each silver pin became a star in the embroidered night sky.

names.legendary: Cardovius, Joker of the Last Hand

lore.common: Slips out of the deck when someone is about to shuffle, then hides beneath the sofa.
lore.uncommon: Changes its corner crease so that it looks like a different card each game.
lore.rare: Appears in a magician's pocket no matter which card the audience picked. The magician is furious.
lore.epic: Turned every card at a tournament into an ace at once. The players argued for seven hours and eventually declared the dealer king.
lore.legendary: Cardovius once dealt a single hand to a tyrant and a beggar. By dawn their fortunes had reversed, and the joker was nowhere to be found.

names.legendary: Folioria, Builder of the Paper Kingdom

lore.common: Loses a cardboard tab every time an eager little finger tries to make the knight wave.
lore.uncommon: Unfolds a tiny dragon that sneezes paper confetti into the reader's face.
lore.rare: Raises an entire castle from a single page, complete with guards who demand to see library cards.
lore.epic: Opened at a school assembly and built a sprawling paper city across the hall. The head teacher spent the day negotiating with origami traffic wardens.
lore.legendary: Folioria folded an entire refuge for a lost kingdom inside its covers. The people lived there safely until peace returned, and their paper palace still opens for anyone needing shelter.

lore.common: Falls from the refrigerator every time somebody opens the milk door.
lore.uncommon: Hides the best holiday picture behind the one of a particularly boring hotel pool.
lore.rare: Sends the smell of a distant beach into the kitchen whenever an old postcard is read.
lore.epic: Unfurled into a giant wall of holiday greetings across the town square. Every resident found a handwritten message from somebody they missed.
lore.legendary: Postaria carries letters from travellers separated by a thousand years. On quiet evenings its oldest cards reveal places that have vanished from every modern map.

names.legendary: Posterion, Face of the Forgotten Star

lore.common: Peels off the wall at midnight with a slap loud enough to wake the household.
lore.uncommon: Holds on to three corners while the fourth insists on waving at passing visitors.
lore.rare: Steps down from the wall to dance whenever its band comes on the radio.
lore.epic: Replaced every advertisement in the city with the same giant portrait of a smiling hamster. The hamster became an overnight celebrity.
lore.legendary: Posterion displayed a singer so famous that her portrait drew crowds a century after she vanished. Each midnight the printed mouth hums the one song nobody recorded.

lore.common: Rolls itself back up whenever the audience finally gets comfortable.
lore.uncommon: Displays one enormous wrinkle directly across the hero's face.
lore.rare: Catches projected characters in its fabric until they finish telling their stories.
lore.epic: Unrolled across the entire town square and displayed every citizen's most embarrassing school photo at once.
lore.legendary: Veluria once caught a projected moon and kept its silver reflection alive during a hundred moonless nights. The real moon still peers over her edge in jealousy.

lore.common: Measures the corner of your homework, then quietly adds three degrees.
lore.uncommon: Hides under a maths worksheet and leaves every triangle slightly offended.
lore.rare: Bends a perfect right angle into a doorway nobody can walk through straight.
lore.epic: Rewrote every angle in the school building overnight. The corridors now meet at 37 degrees, and the caretaker carries a compass.
lore.legendary: Archimandra measured the curve of a falling star and proved the heavens were crooked. The constellations have been rearranging themselves ever since.

names.legendary: Thumbelthorn, Keeper of a Thousand Notes

lore.common: Waits on the floor with its point upwards like a very small villain.
lore.uncommon: Holds an ancient notice on the board and refuses to let anybody admit the event is over.
lore.rare: Pins a rumour to the noticeboard and makes it appear in every classroom by lunchtime.
lore.epic: Pinned a thundercloud to the school corkboard. The geography class now has its own extremely local weather forecast.
lore.legendary: Thumbelthorn fastened the last words of a dying poet to a sky-sized noticeboard. Whenever the wind turns, another forgotten verse appears.

lore.common: Turns completely blank the moment someone asks for a refund.
lore.uncommon: Hides at the bottom of a pocket and emerges after the washing machine has finished its work.
lore.rare: Remembers every purchase a shopkeeper has conveniently forgotten and prints it in glowing letters.
lore.epic: Returned every overpriced purchase in the city on the same afternoon. The shopkeepers formed a support group.
lore.legendary: Receipta holds the proof of a bargain struck between a mortal and the wind. Once each century she returns one impossible debt, paid in the exact change.

names.legendary: Tillandra, Scroll of the Endless Account

lore.common: Escapes from the till and rolls beneath the counter at top speed.
lore.uncommon: Prints a receipt long enough to wrap around the customer's ankles.
lore.rare: Records everything bought in a shop, including items nobody remembers seeing.
lore.epic: Unspooled from the supermarket till and tangled the entire shopping centre in paper. The manager tried to file it as stationery.
lore.legendary: Tillandra has recorded every transaction of a vanished merchant empire on one unbroken ribbon. The last line still reads ONE MOON, PAID IN FULL.

names.legendary: Stretchella, Who Held the Sky Together

lore.common: Waits until the perfect moment to leap from somebody's fingers and vanish behind a cupboard.
lore.uncommon: Keeps a bundle of letters so tight that they begin telling each other secrets.
lore.rare: Twangs a musical note that sends every paper clip on the desk into a tiny dance.
lore.epic: Bounced a gigantic rubber-band ball through the town square. It returned every hour, each time with a different mayor attached.
lore.legendary: Stretchella stretched herself across a crack in the heavens and kept the stars from spilling out. The constellations still tremble whenever someone snaps a band.

lore.common: Uses its chipped edge to turn every straight line into a suspiciously cheerful wave.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to admit that the centimetre marks on its side are slightly uneven.
lore.rare: Measures a shadow and makes it longer than the object that cast it. The geometry teacher resigns.
lore.epic: Announced that every desk was exactly one centimetre too small, then expanded all the classrooms to fit. The school gates no longer close.
lore.legendary: Inchworth measured the distance between the Moon and a child's bedroom window using one battered wooden ruler. Every night the Moon moves a little closer to hear the results.

names.legendary: Saint Claspina, Binder of Broken Banners

lore.common: Pricks its owner whenever they call it harmless.
lore.uncommon: Saves a torn trouser hem minutes before the school photograph, then demands a medal.
lore.rare: Appears in a pocket whenever a costume tears, as if summoned by sheer embarrassment.
lore.epic: Held together every costume in a royal pageant after a jealous moth ate the seams. The moth was assigned to the hat department.
lore.legendary: Saint Claspina bound the shattered flags of a defeated army into one great banner. At dawn the army marched home together, still wearing extremely mismatched uniforms.

lore.common: Glues together the only two pages anyone wanted to look at.
lore.uncommon: Hoards old tickets, petals and ribbon scraps, then demands an explanation for every one.
lore.rare: Opens to the exact page that recalls a forgotten friend. A faded ticket suddenly smells like the seaside.
lore.epic: Spilled every photograph of a family's holiday into the air at once. The images arranged themselves into a moving picture of the best day.
lore.legendary: Pastelwick planted one pressed flower between pages so old that its owner had forgotten the garden. By morning the flower had grown into a path leading home.

names.legendary: Euclidia, Mistress of the Perfect Corner

lore.common: Pokes through the pencil case and draws a tiny triangle on somebody's lunch wrapper.
lore.uncommon: Secretly measures everything on the desk and reports when a sandwich is not exactly square.
lore.rare: Straightens bent picture frames merely by glaring through its transparent triangular body.
lore.epic: Forced every corner in the school into a perfect right angle. The football went square, the clocks got corners and the pizzas were furious.
lore.legendary: Euclidia once squared the winding labyrinth of a spiteful king, revealing a straight path to its heart. The minotaur now teaches geometry and refuses to draw circles.

lore.common: Hides in the carpet and emerges precisely when someone walks barefoot to the kettle.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to accept thread until it hears three compliments about its tiny eye.
lore.rare: Can stitch the split seam of a tent while its owner sleeps, then leaves a neat little signature.
lore.epic: Sewed the cracks in a castle's walls overnight with one strand of golden thread. The builders opened a tailoring shop instead.
lore.legendary: Needlith threaded the scattered stars through a celestial needle's eye and stitched the first constellation into the night. Her knot is still visible at the end of Orion's belt.

lore.common: Chews three sheets, jams on the fourth and asks for someone to empty its belly.
lore.uncommon: Turns an important memo into party confetti just as the manager walks past.
lore.rare: Can shred a secret so thoroughly that the people who wrote it forget the password.
lore.epic: Gobbled a mountain of forms during tax season, and the town declared an unscheduled public holiday. The accountants threw a confetti parade.
lore.legendary: Shredmora devoured the tyrant's endless rulebook page by page until no unjust decree remained. To this day, every blank strip of paper in her nest whispers the word freedom.

lore.common: Grows a tiny moustache on every face drawn in its margins.
lore.uncommon: Gives every hastily drawn dog six legs and a surprisingly judgmental expression.
lore.rare: Lets a sketch of a lost pet climb out of the page for one afternoon, then return with muddy pawprints.
lore.epic: Released an entire pencil-drawn zoo into the art classroom. The elephants were made of triangles and the teacher had to erase the doors.
lore.legendary: Sketchara keeps a second world between her blank pages, where every abandoned idea gets a home. When a young artist opens the final page, a sunrise is waiting to be drawn.

lore.common: Gets hot when nobody needs it and cold exactly when the wire must be fixed.
lore.uncommon: Leaves tiny silver solder footprints across the workshop bench overnight.
lore.rare: Reconnects any broken circuit with a touch, including the old radio that speaks only in grandad's voice.
lore.epic: Welded every streetlight into a single musical circuit. The city now plays a different chord whenever somebody crosses the road.
lore.legendary: Solderon reunited two pieces of a shattered star with one shining seam. Astronomers have argued about the solder mark ever since.

lore.common: Paints the dog's fur blue every time a sunbeam crosses the living-room floor.
lore.uncommon: Holds its coloured shards together like an argumentative jigsaw puzzle.
lore.rare: Casts living shapes of light across the walls, where they dance until the sun moves on.
lore.epic: Turned the entire cathedral into a walking rainbow at noon; the stained-glass saints stepped off the windows to join the parade.
lore.legendary: Vitrealia captured seven different dawns in one shattered window. Those who stand beneath it may glimpse a morning they thought they had lost.

names.legendary: Styloria, the Hand Beyond the Glass

lore.common: Draws a moustache on every portrait and blames a greasy fingerprint.
lore.uncommon: Clicks against screens like a woodpecker with a design degree.
lore.rare: Draws doors in tablet pictures, then lets little illustrated creatures escape for lunch.
lore.epic: Sketched a staircase off the edge of a screen; every character in the game climbed into the room to demand better dialogue.
lore.legendary: Styloria writes in light on the surface of dreams. One stroke of its silent pen restored a lost city's memories to the blank tablets in its museum.

lore.common: Sneezes a century of dust whenever anyone tries to straighten its hem.
lore.uncommon: Changes one tiny embroidered face so the knight looks suspiciously like the baker.
lore.rare: Lets stitched heroes escape from the wall to settle historical arguments in person.
lore.epic: Unfurled across the fortress and rewove an ancient battle, replacing every charging knight with a triumphant flock of geese.
lore.legendary: Arachnevia weaves memories the historians erased. In her endless hanging, the forgotten are never reduced to names; they rise each night to finish their stories.

names.legendary: Thimbor, Shield of the Thousand Stitches

lore.common: Gets stuck on the wrong finger just as the sewing begins.
lore.uncommon: Clinks against the needle like a tiny knight challenging a dragon.
lore.rare: Turns even the bluntest sewing needle into a perfectly guided silver dart through thick cloth.
lore.epic: Protected the royal tailors as they stitched a sail large enough to catch a hurricane. Not a single finger was pricked.
lore.legendary: Thimbor once defended a village of tiny seamstresses from a rain of falling needles. His dented silver shell hangs in their great hall as a battle shield.

lore.common: Gets lost in the sewing tin between two enormous buttons.
lore.uncommon: Serves a complete afternoon tea to a family of dolls and one very polite beetle.
lore.rare: Turns into a tiny silver helmet for any brave insect about to explore the garden.
lore.epic: Was carried to the beach by a beetle army and used to raise a sand fortress above the incoming tide.
lore.legendary: Minithim saved a ship of toy sailors with a thousand trips of water in its little silver cup. The smallest hero in the harbour still has the biggest statue.

names.legendary: Tackoria, Fastener of the Falling Sky

lore.common: Lies point-up exactly where the person taking off their shoes will step.
lore.uncommon: Moves important notes to the corner of the board nobody ever reads.
lore.rare: Pins shadows to walls so the owners have to come back to collect them.
lore.epic: Fired a thousand bright tacks into the school noticeboard, pinning up every missing poster and forgotten permission slip at once.
lore.legendary: Tackoria fixed a loose star to the heavens with a silver pin when it began to fall. The constellation has worn that tiny shining point ever since.

lore.common: Disappears from the pocket exactly when the conductor approaches.
lore.uncommon: Tears itself neatly in half and insists both pieces deserve admission.
lore.rare: Wins every raffle it enters, but always awards the prize to someone else.
lore.epic: Printed a golden ticket for every citizen during the grand opening, then magically moved the venue to the wrong street.
lore.legendary: Passaron guards the one seat at every performance kept for someone who never returned. On rare nights the ticket glows, and the curtain rises for a reunion.

names.legendary: Clippard, the Pin That Held the Wind

lore.common: Grips the tie firmly until the wearer bends over the soup. Then it takes a break.
lore.uncommon: Polishes itself during speeches so the audience watches a tiny dancing reflection.
lore.rare: Pins a wayward tie so firmly that even a hurricane cannot tug it free. The wearer may still go flying.
lore.epic: Clamped every dignitary's tie to the banquet table during a state dinner, preventing a walkout and accidentally securing a peace treaty.
lore.legendary: Clippard once caught the trailing thread of a thunderstorm and fastened it to a church spire. The town enjoyed seven days of motionless rain and extraordinarily precise gardening.

lore.common: Hides in a sandwich and pokes out just as someone takes a bite.
lore.uncommon: Wears an olive as a helmet at fancy parties and refuses to remove it.
lore.rare: Extracts microscopic splinters from anything, including a king's wooden throne and the royal family tree.
lore.epic: Built a bristling fortress of cocktail sticks through the wedding buffet. Guests needed tiny catapults to reach the cheese.
lore.legendary: Toothprick is the last splinter of a legendary cedar that held together the first bridge. Though smaller than a fingernail, it can pin the shadow of a falling mountain to the earth.

names.legendary: Cardivus, the Myth in the Last Pack

lore.common: Loses a corner during its first playground trade. It calls the damage battle experience.
lore.uncommon: Shimmers with holographic colours whenever someone mentions its market value.
lore.rare: Leaps from one collector's binder to another and returns with the rarest card in its teeth.
lore.epic: Escaped its sleeve during a tournament and summoned the painted monster into the hall. The referee immediately called for a rematch.
lore.legendary: Cardivus was drawn onto a single card by an artist who never finished the eyes. Every century it awakens to choose a new champion, and each champion sees a different creature staring back.

lore.common: Puffs a cloud into everyone's personal space and acts astonished when they move.
lore.uncommon: Smells like a candy factory arguing with a burnt toaster.
lore.rare: Fogs an entire bus shelter while the people inside vote to ban it.
lore.epic: Wrapped the rush-hour platform in a sickly strawberry mist. Commuters emerged on the wrong trains, still complaining about the smell.
lore.legendary: Claimed it could command the weather with one breath. The real clouds sent a thunderstorm to remind it what fresh air looks like.

lore.common: Tilts itself sideways whenever somebody straightens it.
lore.uncommon: Insists its upside-down side is the expensive side.
lore.rare: Changes its painted expression to comment on the visitors' outfits.
lore.epic: Walked out of its frame at a museum opening and swapped places with the curator. The critics called it revolutionary.
lore.legendary: Was thrown away by a cleaner and immediately became the most celebrated artwork of its century. Its new exhibition includes the bin, which demands royalties.

lore.common: Keeps the ghost of last week's meeting under three coats of eraser dust.
lore.uncommon: Eats every marker ink except the bright yellow nobody can read.
lore.rare: Erases unfinished homework just before the teacher turns around.
lore.epic: Filled itself with so many impossible ideas that they climbed off the board as tiny chalky creatures and ran the company for a day.
lore.legendary: Held the final theorem of a vanished mathematician beneath a hundred years of eraser marks. When a child drew the right first line, the entire proof wrote itself in dancing ink.
